data.body:
A TOML descriptor loaded into the RecordKind registry (P-record-contract, P-extension-seams.registry); Python only for kinds with behaviour; about 15 new kinds (requirement, stakeholder, vendor, contract, risk, comm log, assumption, fitness function, proposal types, attestation, attention item) become rows; user-defined kinds follow; conformance test (B-rc-conformance) runs over data kinds too.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

Split into: SE-kind-data.1, SE-kind-data.2, SE-kind-data.3.

chunk_findings.detail: `records.py` executes `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` (and immediately calls `load_packaged("rule")`) while `record_kind_data` is still mid-import, so the two modules can only be imported in the order "records first". Given the reverse order, the chain is: `import ddflow.api.record_kind_data` → its top-level `from . import records as R` starts executing `records.py` → `records.py` reaches `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` → `record_kind_data` is in `sys.modules` but partially initialized (`load_packaged` is defined *after* the `from . import records` line, so it has not been bound yet) → CPython raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'load_packaged' from partially initialized module 'ddflow.api.record_kind_data' (most likely due to a circular import)`. Concretely, `python -c "import ddflow.api.record_kind_data"` — or any test/loader module whose first ddflow import is `from ddflow.api.record_kind_data import parse_kind, packaged`, which is the natural way to exercise this new file — fails at import time as long as `ddflow/api/__init__.py` does not itself import `records` first. Placing the import mid-file with `# noqa: E402` only satisfies the linter; it does not break the cycle. Moving the `records` import inside the three functions (or having `records` import `load_packaged` lazily inside a function rather than at module scope) would remove the order dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py:26 (`from . import records as R`)

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring states the loader's central safety invariant: "Python is for kinds with behaviour (`ops`, `weakening`); a descriptor naming either is refused." Nothing in the diff enforces this. `kind_from_data` copies the parsed descriptor verbatim (`args = dict(desc)`), rewrites only `fields`, `declined`, `export` and `feed`, and then calls `R.RecordKind(**args)`. Since `RecordKind` is the same class that behaviour kinds use to carry `ops`/`weakening` (the docstring itself implies these keys are nameable on this structure), a descriptor such as `ops = ["ddflow.something"]` or `weakening = true` is not refused — it is accepted and passed straight into the kind, i.e. a data-only TOML descriptor can smuggle in the behaviour the loader is documented to keep in Python. The stated refusal is a check that was never written, so the guarantee callers will rely on ("a kind with no behaviour needs no Python") does not hold for these two keys.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py (`kind_from_data`, module docstring)

chunk_findings.detail: `D.register_kind(args["def_kind"], args["summary"])` is invoked *before* `R.RecordKind(**args)`, and `register_kind` mutates the global `defs.DEF_KINDS` via `setdefault`. Any descriptor that gets past the field/verb/export rewriting but then fails construction (e.g. an unexpected key such as `bogus = "x"`, or a missing required `name`, making `RecordKind(**args)` raise `TypeError`) has already permanently added its `def_kind` to `DEF_KINDS`. Concrete input: `parse_kind('name="?" ...')` on a descriptor whose only problem is an extra key leaves `defs.DEF_KINDS["<new def_kind>"]` present even though no kind was ever declared and the caller saw an exception; a subsequent parse of a corrected descriptor, or any later code that trusts `DEF_KINDS`, now sees a definition kind that was never successfully created. Moving the registration after successful construction (or rolling it back on failure) would remove the failed-parse leak.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py:54 (`kind_from_data` -> `D.register_kind`)

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier report stands: `record_kind_data.py` does `from . import records as R` at module scope, and `records.py` executes `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` at module scope and immediately calls it. Whichever module is imported first forces the other to be executed while the first is still partially initialized. Concretely, `python -c "import ddflow.api.record_kind_data"` starts executing `record_kind_data.py`, reaches line 26, runs `records.py`, which reaches `from .record_kind_data import load_packaged` against the partially-initialized module — resolving only if `load_packaged` happens to be bound above line 26; otherwise this raises ImportError, so the two modules are only importable in the order "records first". The triage for this item is still `untriaged` and the portion of the diff shown here (the new `ddflow/templates/kinds/rule.toml` descriptor) contains no change to either module, so nothing in this part of the change answers the finding.

chunk_findings.detail: The two file-discovery helpers in this new module disagree about what a descriptor's "name" is, so composing them the obvious way fails at runtime. `packaged()` yields `entry.name`, i.e. the file name including the extension (`"<name>.toml"`, per its own docstring "`(file name, text)` of every packaged descriptor"), whereas `load_packaged(name)` builds its path as `KINDS_DIR / f"{name}.toml"`, i.e. it expects the bare kind name. Given the packaged descriptors on disk, a caller that enumerates `for fname, text in packaged(): load_packaged(fname)` (the natural way to load everything the module advertises) reads `ddflow/templates/kinds/<name>.toml.toml` and raises `FileNotFoundError`, and there is nothing in either signature or docstring that tells the caller to strip the suffix. Either `packaged()` should yield `entry.stem`, or `load_packaged` should accept a name that may already carry `.toml`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_kind_data.py `packaged()` / `load_packaged()`

chunk_findings.detail: `re.search(v.pattern, item[:MAX_VALUE])` matches only the first 20000 characters, so a pattern validator is silently not enforced on the rest of the value. Input: a kind with `render = "{title}"` and `[[validator]] field="slug", pattern="^[a-z]+$"`; a record with `slug = "a" * 20000 + "!"`. `item[:MAX_VALUE]` is 20000 `a`s, `^[a-z]+$` matches, `_value_problem` returns `""`, and the record is accepted although the stored value contains `!`, which the declared pattern forbids. Rejecting values longer than the bound (or matching the whole value) would be correct; truncating turns a bound on pathological input into a validation bypass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:135-142 (`_value_problem`, pattern check)

chunk_findings.detail: The `if n` filter drops the empty field name produced by an auto-numbered format field, so both the declaration check and `render` ignore it. A template such as `render = "{}"` (or `"{:>10}"`) yields `used = set()` in `declaration_problems`, which therefore reports no problem, but `render()` builds `data` with no positional entry (names is empty, so there is no `"0"` key) and `rules.render.format_map(data)` raises (IndexError/KeyError for the positional lookup) instead of returning a string. Input: a kind descriptor with `render = "{}"`; `declaration_problems({...})` returns `[]`, and `render(rules, "r1", "open", {"title": "t"})` raises at render time rather than surfacing a declaration error (contrast `"{0}"`, which is flagged as naming no such field).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:110-113 and 194-201 (`declaration_problems` / `render`, positional fields)

chunk_findings.detail: In the show payload the record's field values are carried nested (the very next expression reads `data.get("fields")`), yet the lifecycle state handed to the renderer is read from the top level with `str(data.get("status", ""))`. A record's state is one of its fields, so for a kind whose rules declare a render template, e.g. a `bug` record with `data["fields"] == {"status": "fixed", ...}`, `data.get("status", "")` evaluates to `""`, not `"fixed"`. `KR.render` is therefore invoked for the empty/unknown state, and every `show` of a rules-bearing record returns a `rendered` string computed from the wrong state (e.g. the default-state branch of the template instead of the branch selected by the record's actual status). The correct source is the same mapping already being passed as `fields`, i.e. `(data.get("fields") or {}).get("status", "")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/records.py:496 (show path, `data["rendered"] = KR.render(...)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The allowed-key set is computed from `t.get("transitions", {})` *before* `_tab` validates that value, so a non-iterable `transitions` value escapes the module's error contract. Descriptor input `[kind.lifecycle] field = "state" initial = "new" transitions = 5` raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` out of `set(...)` instead of the documented `RulesError`. Every other malformed declaration in this file (bad table, bad state list, bad `sources`, bad `stamp`) is reported as `RulesError`; a caller that does `try: from_raw(...) except RulesError: <report config error>` will instead propagate an unexpected TypeError and abort on a merely malformed kind descriptor. (`transitions = 5.5` and `transitions = true` hit the same path.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:from_raw (`_tab("lifecycle.transitions", t.get("transitions", {}), set(t.get("transitions", {})))`)

chunk_findings.detail: Fields used by `sources` and by `pattern`/`max_length` validators are never constrained to a string type, so declarations that cannot work pass the "does not fit" check, and the runtime check then behaves wrongly. Two concrete inputs: (1) a kind whose field `code` has type `integer` with `[[validator]] field = "code" pattern = "^[0-9]{4}$"` — `declaration_problems` returns `[]`, and `_value_problem` skips every non-`str` item, so `{"code": 12345}` is stored with the pattern silently never enforced (same for `max_length` on a non-string field); (2) a kind whose integer field `revision` is listed in `sources` — `declaration_problems` returns `[]`, but `_sources_problem` computes `blank = not fields.get(name) or ...`, so a record with `{"revision": 0}` (a filled field) is rejected with "revision is required: a record cites its source", while `False`/`[]` behave the same way. Both would be closed by requiring `"string"` for `sources` and for `pattern`/`max_length` validators, as the lifecycle and link checks already do.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:KindRules.declaration_problems (`need("sources", name)` and `want = ("integer",) if ... else ()`)

chunk_findings.detail: `declaration_problems` still treats a validator as numeric-only whenever `v.min is not None or v.max is not None`: the `numeric` branch wins and the pattern/max_length branch is unreachable, so a validator carrying *both* a bound and a text constraint is only checked for the integer field type. Input: kind field `code` declared `type = "integer"`, plus `[[validator]] field = "code" min = 1 pattern = "^[0-9]{4}$"`. `declaration_problems` returns `[]` (`want == ("integer",)`), and at runtime `_value_problem({"code": 12345})` calls `_bounds_problem` (passes, `12345 >= 1`), then reaches `items = [12345]`, where `isinstance(i, str)` is false, so `_text_problem` never runs and the pattern is silently never enforced — `{"code": 12345}` and `{"code": 999999}` are both stored. The identical hole exists for `max_length` combined with a bound (`min = 1 max_length = 4` accepts an integer of any length), which is exactly the "declaration that cannot work passes the check, and the runtime check then behaves wrongly" failure the confirmed finding described; the fix only closes the case where no bound is present.

chunk_findings.detail: The refutation of finding #1 is asserted by `tests/test_kind_data_rules.py::test_show_renders_status_as_the_definition_status`, but that probe does not exercise the path the finding was about, and the code that decides the outcome is not in this delta (this is part 2/2; the show path in `ddflow/api/records.py` is in the unseen part 1). The probe builds a `risk` kind whose record has no field named `status`, so `{status}` is resolved from the envelope's definition status (`"active"`) and the assert `"r1 is active"` holds under *both* the old expression `str(data.get("status", ""))` and any repaired version — the finding's concrete input was a kind whose lifecycle field *is* named `status` (or a template that renders the state, `{state}`), and the test never renders `{state}` nor declares a `status` field. Concretely: a kind with `[lifecycle] field = "status"` and a record in state `fixed` plus a template `"bug is {status}"` will still print the definition status, not `fixed`, if the render namespace merges the top-level envelope after the nested `fields` (or if the renderer only ever sees the top-level dict, which is exactly what the probe's single assertion cannot rule out). So from this delta the refutation is "cannot be verified": the probe passes either way and the implementation being claimed as correct is not shown here. (Findings #2 and #3 are different: their added probes assert error messages — `"transitions must be a table"`, `"sources field 'n' is a integer"`, `"validator field 'n'"` — that the previously reported code could not have produced, so those are treated as answered.)

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:KindRules.declaration_problems (`need("sources", name)` and `want = ("integer",) if ... else ()`)

chunk_findings.detail: `declaration_problems` still treats a validator as numeric-only whenever `v.min is not None or v.max is not None`: the `numeric` branch wins and the pattern/max_length branch is unreachable, so a validator carrying *both* a bound and a text constraint is only checked for the integer field type. Input: kind field `code` declared `type = "integer"`, plus `[[validator]] field = "code" min = 1 pattern = "^[0-9]{4}$"`. `declaration_problems` returns `[]` (`want == ("integer",)`), and at runtime `_value_problem({"code": 12345})` calls `_bounds_problem` (passes, `12345 >= 1`), then reaches `items = [12345]`, where `isinstance(i, str)` is false, so `_text_problem` never runs and the pattern is silently never enforced — `{"code": 12345}` and `{"code": 999999}` are both stored. The identical hole exists for `max_length` combined with a bound (`min = 1 max_length = 4` accepts an integer of any length), which is exactly the "declaration that cannot work passes the check, and the runtime check then behaves wrongly" failure the confirmed finding described; the fix only closes the case where no bound is present.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:96 (`want = (...) if numeric else ("string", "array") if (v.pattern or v.max_length)`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:96 (`want = (...) if numeric else ("string", "array") if (v.pattern or v.max_length)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The refutation of finding #1 is asserted by `tests/test_kind_data_rules.py::test_show_renders_status_as_the_definition_status`, but that probe does not exercise the path the finding was about, and the code that decides the outcome is not in this delta (this is part 2/2; the show path in `ddflow/api/records.py` is in the unseen part 1). The probe builds a `risk` kind whose record has no field named `status`, so `{status}` is resolved from the envelope's definition status (`"active"`) and the assert `"r1 is active"` holds under *both* the old expression `str(data.get("status", ""))` and any repaired version — the finding's concrete input was a kind whose lifecycle field *is* named `status` (or a template that renders the state, `{state}`), and the test never renders `{state}` nor declares a `status` field. Concretely: a kind with `[lifecycle] field = "status"` and a record in state `fixed` plus a template `"bug is {status}"` will still print the definition status, not `fixed`, if the render namespace merges the top-level envelope after the nested `fields` (or if the renderer only ever sees the top-level dict, which is exactly what the probe's single assertion cannot rule out). So from this delta the refutation is "cannot be verified": the probe passes either way and the implementation being claimed as correct is not shown here. (Findings #2 and #3 are different: their added probes assert error messages — `"transitions must be a table"`, `"sources field 'n' is a integer"`, `"validator field 'n'"` — that the previously reported code could not have produced, so those are treated as answered.)

titles: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:96 (`want = (...) if numeric else ("string", "array") if (v.pattern or v.max_length)`)

chunk_findings.detail: `re.search(v.pattern, item[:MAX_VALUE])` matches only the first 20000 characters, so a pattern validator is silently not enforced on the rest of the value. Input: a kind with `render = "{title}"` and `[[validator]] field="slug", pattern="^[a-z]+$"`; a record with `slug = "a" * 20000 + "!"`. `item[:MAX_VALUE]` is 20000 `a`s, `^[a-z]+$` matches, `_value_problem` returns `""`, and the record is accepted although the stored value contains `!`, which the declared pattern forbids. Rejecting values longer than the bound (or matching the whole value) would be correct; truncating turns a bound on pathological input into a validation bypass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:135-142 (`_value_problem`, pattern check)

chunk_findings.detail: The `if n` filter drops the empty field name produced by an auto-numbered format field, so both the declaration check and `render` ignore it. A template such as `render = "{}"` (or `"{:>10}"`) yields `used = set()` in `declaration_problems`, which therefore reports no problem, but `render()` builds `data` with no positional entry (names is empty, so there is no `"0"` key) and `rules.render.format_map(data)` raises (IndexError/KeyError for the positional lookup) instead of returning a string. Input: a kind descriptor with `render = "{}"`; `declaration_problems({...})` returns `[]`, and `render(rules, "r1", "open", {"title": "t"})` raises at render time rather than surfacing a declaration error (contrast `"{0}"`, which is flagged as naming no such field).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/kindrules.py:110-113 and 194-201 (`declaration_problems` / `render`, positional fields)
